extracted.intended_audience: parliamentary select committee and colonial administrators (Governor‑General and Council)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts from late‑18th century letters and evidence outlining principles and recommendations for administering the Carnatic revenues, leasing districts, and protecting renters during wartime and political disorder. Focuses on expense reduction, lease procedures, distinctions between military and civil charges, and protections for third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of expenses and change of principal aumildars
rubrics_metrics.description: We proposed a considerable and immediate reduction of expenses, and a total change of the principal aumildars who had been employed under the Nabob.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action recommended because ordinary expenses were rated on an extravagant scale; authors preferred to risk retrenching too much rather than too little since it is easier to add allowances later than to diminish them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of renters under the Company's sole authority & public advertisement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended that such of the Nabob's districts as were in a state to be farmed out might be immediately let by a public advertisement, issued in the Company's name, and circulated through every province of the Carnatic; advertised for the whole period of the Nabob's assignment, with the security of the Company's protection promised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This plan encouraged bidders, produced numerous proposals and favourable terms, and was shown necessary by attempts to counteract it. Promising Company's protection was used to encourage participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminate expense categories and preserve legitimate customs
rubrics_metrics.description: Be careful to discriminate those charges incurred for troops (defence) from those of the sibbendy, servants, etc., for cultivation and revenue collection; pay attention to established customs, ancient privileges of the inhabitants, and public charities which should be continued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid blending diverse items under one confused title (which permitted concealment, appropriation, fraud and oppression). Continue necessary customary allowances but prevent inflated or conflated expense accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retract extraordinary sibbendies/sepoys and enlist where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Receive such of these people as will enlist into the Company's service, and discharge the rest; every charge under that head has been struck out of our account of expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enlisting reduces extraordinary charges, relieves country of burden, and helps fix the Company's authority necessary for due revenue collection; any additions to Company establishment later should be deducted from current savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservative retrenchment policy (err on greater cuts)
rubrics_metrics.description: We have not acted sparingly, but chose rather, in cases of doubt, to incur the hazard of retrenching too much than too little; because it would be easier, after any stated allowance for expenses, to add what might be necessary than to diminish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical rule for budgeting during reform: prefer over‑correction initially to allow later restorations rather than undercutting needed savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect legal integrity of leases and protect renters (third‑party protections)
rubrics_metrics.description: The renters applied to this government in consequence of public advertisements... have entered into mutual and strict covenants with us; by which covenants... we and our constituents, and the public faith, are in like manner bound to maintain them in the enjoyment of their leases during the continuance of the term. Their leases cannot be legally torn from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before ordering surrender of the assignment consider how it will affect third persons who have not breached engagements; arbitrary removal would be oppressive and a breach of public faith. Provide protections to renters before exposing them to Nabob's ministers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid language manipulation and ensure faithful communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Changing the Nabob's correspondence from Persian to English gave Mr. Benfield the opportunity to relate and read what he pleased to the Amir-ul-Omrah; the Nabob could sign papers he did not understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not substitute or manipulate official language/translations to gain ascendency over native rulers; ensure truthful translations and direct channels to prevent deception and abuse of authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer local managers acquainted with district customs
rubrics_metrics.description: When let to persons who were strangers to the manners and customs of the people, they oppressed the inhabitants, many left the country, and deserted cultivation; as a result the farmers were disappointed and failed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letting to local aumildars or persons acquainted with the district is preferable; outsiders unfamiliar with local customs risk oppression, desertion, and collapse of collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess ability to pay before demanding large sums
rubrics_metrics.description: Government should desire the Rajah to make up a statement of his accounts, disbursements, debts, and payments to the Company, in order to ascertain whether the country was able to pay increasing demands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to demand or reason upon such statements led to unreasonable demands; adapt financial demands to the true capacity of the province or ruler to avoid ruinous impositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve agricultural inputs and critical infrastructure (seed advances, mounds, Anicut)
rubrics_metrics.description: The king of Tanjore, as proprietor of the land, always makes advances of money for seed for the cultivation of the land. A considerable annual expense is necessary to keep up mounds and watercourses and the Anicut; neglect will partially supply water, overflow some districts, parch others, and generally injure the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that extorting money beyond capacity can prevent seed provision and infrastructure repairs, leading to uncultivated lands and long‑term loss; maintain these expenditures as essential to revenue and prosperity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare lease rents with Nabob's accounts and verify actual produce
rubrics_metrics.description: Lay before your Lordship the statement of sums at which the districts were let, compared with the accounts of their produce delivered by the Nabob. The Nabob's accounts may state sums which former renters engaged to pay, and not what was actually produced by the districts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparative statements to detect discrepancies between nominal rents and actual produce; do not rely uncritically on Nabob's ledgered figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect limited immediate fulfillment during wartime but minimize collection losses
rubrics_metrics.description: Your Lordship cannot expect, in the midst of danger, invasion, and distress, that the renters now appointed will be able at present to fulfil the terms of their leases; but we trust, from measures we have taken, that very little, if any, of the actual collections will be lost, even during the war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When leasing in unstable times, anticipate underperformance; mitigate through measures (protection, careful selection) to preserve as much collection as possible and rely on full performance on return of peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid attempting settlements under enemy occupation; gather information first
rubrics_metrics.description: The situation of the Arcot province will not admit of the same settlement which has been made for the other districts; the enemy being in possession of the capital and having entirely desolated the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defer similar leasing/administrative settlements where the enemy occupies territory; instead obtain available information and propose arrangements when conditions permit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Company protection to calm local apprehensions and encourage engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: A man seized by the Nabob's sepoys within Madras gave alarm, and government found it necessary to promise the protection of the Company, in order to calm the apprehensions of the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offering protection is necessary to reassure native applicants and secure their participation in leases and administration; failure to protect discourages offers and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider borrowings and usurious interest when imposing financial demands
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rajah was obliged to borrow at most exorbitant interest (some at 48%) to pay instalments; large demands forced ruinous lending at high rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When setting rents or large demands, account for likely recourse to costly borrowing by the debtor; unreasonable demands may compel ruinous loans and undermine repayment capacity.
